journey.title: Apply for or renew a U.S. passport
journey.summary: Choose the renewal or in-person route that fits your passport, prepare the right documents, and submit directly to the State Department.
eligibility: Choose the age-specific application if you cannot renew. Passports issued before age 16 cannot be renewed.
These submission steps are for applicants in the United States. Use the official embassy or consulate instructions when applying abroad.

steps.title: Choose online, mail, or in-person service
steps.detail: Online renewal requires age 25+, a ten-year passport expiring within one year or expired less than five years, no personal-information changes, possession of an undamaged passport not reported lost or stolen, and no travel for at least six weeks. Check the official document-combination rules too. Mail renewal generally requires a ten-year passport issued at age 16+ within the last 15 years, undamaged and never reported lost or stolen, with any required legal name-change evidence. Otherwise use the age-specific in-person application.

steps.title: Prepare the documents for your route
steps.detail: Mail: complete and sign DS-82, include your previous passport, one compliant photo, and any required name-change evidence. Online: keep your passport and prepare a digital photo. In person: use DS-11 and the age-specific citizenship, ID, photocopy, and photo checklist; sign when the acceptance agent tells you.
requirements: Mail: DS-82, previous passport, photo, and payment.
Online: passport, digital photo, and payment card.
In person: DS-11 and the official document checklist for your age.

steps.title: Check the fee and payment method
steps.detail: Choose a book, card, or both and confirm the current total for your route. In-person applications also have an acceptance fee.
fees: Adult renewal: $130 book, $30 card, or $160 for both.
Optional services and in-person acceptance can add fees. Use the current official calculator.

steps.title: Submit through your chosen official channel
steps.detail: For mail renewal, use the current mailing address for your residence and service speed. Online renewal is submitted personally at opr.travel.state.gov; keep your old passport, which becomes invalid for travel. For DS-11, attend the required acceptance appointment.

steps.title: Plan for processing and delivery
steps.detail: Processing and mailing are separate. Confirm the current service times before booking travel and use the urgent-travel instructions when ordinary service is too slow.
deadlines: Online renewal requires no international travel for at least six weeks after submission.
For urgent travel, check passport-agency appointment eligibility immediately.

journey.title: Get a California driver's license after moving
journey.summary: For an adult with a valid out-of-state license: prepare your documents, start the application, and finish at a California DMV office.
audience: Adult California residents with a valid out-of-state driver's license
eligibility: This route covers adults with a valid license from another U.S. state.
Under 18, first-time drivers, foreign licenses, AB 60, and commercial licenses have different requirements; choose the official route for your situation.

steps.title: Confirm your license route
steps.detail: Check California residency and select your license type. Vehicle registration is a separate task if you bring a car.

steps.title: Gather identity and residency documents
steps.detail: Use the DMV list for your chosen standard or REAL ID license. Prepare original or certified identity evidence, residency documents if you have never had a California DL/ID, and your Social Security number for the official DMV application.
requirements: Acceptable original or certified identity document.
Acceptable California residency documents when required.
Social Security number, entered only on the official DMV application.

steps.title: Start the application online
steps.detail: Create or sign in to your DMV account, submit the DL/ID application, and keep its confirmation. The application still needs to be completed at a field office.

steps.title: Finish at a DMV office
steps.detail: Bring the required documents and confirmation. Pay the application fee and complete the required identity, photo, thumbprint, vision, and knowledge checks.
fees: The application fee depends on license type; check the fee link in the official DMV requirements.
deadlines: A submitted online application does not by itself authorize driving. Confirm the residency and licensing rules before driving.

journey.title: Transfer an out-of-state driver's license to Texas
journey.summary: For adults with a valid U.S. state license: complete vehicle prerequisites, prepare documents, and apply at Texas DPS.
audience: Texas residents age 18+ with a valid, unexpired U.S. state driver's license
eligibility: This route covers adults transferring a valid, unexpired noncommercial license from another U.S. state.
Minors, learner permits, expired licenses, foreign licenses, and commercial licenses need their own DPS instructions.

steps.title: Check your transfer eligibility
steps.detail: A qualifying valid license permits driving for up to 90 days after moving. Surrender it when applying; qualifying adults do not take knowledge or skills exams.
deadlines: Up to 90 days after moving with a qualifying valid, unexpired license.

steps.title: Complete vehicle prerequisites
steps.detail: Register each vehicle you own in Texas before applying. Prepare registration and insurance evidence; if you own no vehicle, provide the required statement.

steps.title: Gather your application documents
steps.detail: Use the DPS document checklist for citizenship or lawful presence, identity, Texas residency, and Social Security number. Enter sensitive information only on official applications.
requirements: Identity and citizenship or lawful-presence evidence.
Texas residency evidence and Social Security number.
Your out-of-state license and applicable vehicle documents.

steps.title: Apply at your DPS appointment
steps.detail: Schedule through the DPS appointment link. Bring the completed application and documents, surrender your license, pay the applicable fee, and complete photo, signature, thumbprint, and vision checks. Review the temporary license for errors.
fees: Check the current fee through the DPS application page.

journey.title: Surrender New York vehicle plates before changing insurance
journey.summary: Return New York plates and registration before canceling New York liability coverage when registering your car in another state.
audience: Owners of New York-registered passenger cars moving their registration to another state
eligibility: This route covers passenger cars with New York plates available to return.
Motorcycles, trailers, and lost or stolen plates have separate instructions.

steps.title: Keep New York coverage until surrender
steps.detail: Out-of-state insurance does not cover a New York registration for DMV purposes. Surrender New York plates and registration before ending New York liability coverage.

steps.title: Prepare the plates and PD-7
steps.detail: Complete PD-7 for each plate set. Remove frames and fasteners and destroy windshield registration and inspection stickers. For mail returns, update your registration address and arrange mail forwarding.
requirements: Plates without frames or fasteners.
Completed PD-7 for each set.

steps.title: Return the plates and keep the receipt
steps.detail: Mail the plates and PD-7 in an envelope to the current official address, or bring them to a DMV office. Retain the FS-6T receipt. The mail postmark counts as the surrender date.
fees: County motor vehicle offices charge $1 to process surrender.
deadlines: Allow 21 days for a mailed receipt; contact DMV if it does not arrive.

steps.title: Coordinate registration and insurance
steps.detail: After surrender, confirm registration and insurance requirements in the destination state. Keep evidence of surrender and new coverage.

journey.title: Report damaged public property in San Francisco
journey.summary: Report a damaged sidewalk bench, bike rack, parking meter, transit shelter, or another listed public object to San Francisco 311 and track the request.
audience: People reporting a listed damaged public object in San Francisco
eligibility: This route covers the public objects listed by SF311 in San Francisco.
For damaged traffic signals, call 311; parking and traffic signs use a separate report.

steps.title: Describe the object and location
steps.detail: Collect the location, object type, any object identification number, and damage description. Add a photo if available.
requirements: Location and object type.
Object ID, if present, and damage description.
Photo, if available.

steps.title: Submit through SF311
steps.detail: Use the Report link on the official page. Alternatively, call 311 within San Francisco or 415-701-2311 from outside the city; TTY users can call 711.

steps.title: Keep your tracking number
steps.detail: Use the 311 tracking number to follow the case online or in the SF311 app. Response times depend on the object and damage; inspection and repair may differ.

journey.title: Apply for a building permit in unincorporated Los Angeles County
journey.summary: Confirm your project office, prepare plans, and follow the County permit process.
audience: Confirm your project office, prepare plans, and follow the County permit process.

steps.title: Confirm the office
steps.detail: Enter the project address or parcel number in the County Service Locator. Use the returned office; mailing names alone do not establish jurisdiction.

steps.title: Check project requirements
steps.detail: Ask that office which permit type, plans, and approvals your project requires.
requirements: Project location and description.
Plans and attachments required by the office.

steps.title: Submit through EPIC-LA
steps.detail: Create or sign into EPIC-LA. Choose the permit, enter location and contacts, attach required plans, and submit.

steps.title: Complete review and payment
steps.detail: Pay the invoiced review fees and respond to corrections. Complete the required issuance forms.
fees: Project-specific fees are invoiced by the County.

steps.title: Wait for issuance and arrange inspections
steps.detail: Begin permitted work after issuance. Request inspections through EPIC-LA.
steps.caution: Application submission is not permission to start construction.

steps.title: Locate the property
steps.detail: Search the official map using the property address or assessor identification number. Review the zoning and relevant map layers.

steps.title: Confirm applicable rules
steps.detail: Ask a planner about zoning, overlays, and project requirements. Obtain parcel and recorded-document evidence separately.
steps.caution: A zoning map does not establish property rights or grant project approval.

journey.title: Request recorded real-estate documents in Los Angeles County
journey.summary: Request copies of documents recorded with the County recorder.
audience: Request copies of documents recorded with the County recorder.

steps.title: Identify the recorded document
steps.detail: Gather the document title, names, and year or years to search. Confirm the document was recorded in Los Angeles County.
requirements: Document title, names, and recording year or search years.

steps.title: Prepare a written request
steps.detail: Follow the recorder mail instructions. Check the current fee for the document type; prepare a check or money order payable to Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk.

steps.title: Send and retain your request
steps.detail: Send to RR/CC, Real Estate Records, P.O. Box 1130, Norwalk, CA 90651-1130. Allow the official processing period.
deadlines: The recorder lists processing within 20 working days.
